successors.name: Kushan Empire
successors.text: the Mathura region, which 'became part of the Kushan Empire from the reign of Vima Kadphises (90-100 CE)'

ledger.x: c. 144 BCE: the Sakas appear on the Oxus. 'Around 140 BC, eastern Scythians (the Saka, or Sacaraucae of Greek sources)' began invading Parthia and Bactria, apparently pushed by the Yuezhi's southward migration; the Indo-Scythians infobox reads 'c. 150 BCE-400 CE'. -144 is Cliopatria's year.
-126: the Sakas hold Sakastan after killing Phraates II.
-110: the Saka domain reaches its western maximum (57.5E, 25N).

c. 100 BCE: Mithridates II takes Sakastan. Around 100 BC Mithridates II of Parthia defeated the Indo-Scythians and 'the region of Sakastan was incorporated into the Parthian Empire'; the Indo-Scythians page adds that Mithridates II (c. 123-88/87 BCE) seized western Bactria from the Indo-Scythians.

c. 88 BCE: the Sakas settle the Indus. The Indo-Scythians 'established themselves in the Indus around 88 B.C.'; Maues 'seizing Taxila in Punjab, and Gandharas capital city Pushkalavati from the Indo-Greek Kingdoms' (undated there; the Indo-Scythians page has c. 80 BCE).
c. 80 BCE: Maues conquers Gandhara and Taxila. The Indo-Scythians page has him conquer Gandhara and Taxila c. 80 BCE, taking Taxila from Apollodotus II (reign of Maues 85-60 BCE).
-77: the Saka kingdom takes Indo-Greek land inside its +1,000,000 km2 growth.
-77: the Saka kingdom reaches the Gujarat coast.

c. 70 BCE: Mathura falls to the Northern Satraps. 'From around 70 BCE, the region of Mathura fell to the Indo-Scythian Northern Satraps' under Hagamasha and Hagana (the Indo-Scythians page says c. 60 BCE).
ledger.cp: Mathura's local rulers (not named on the page)
Vikrama of Ujjain (no state named on the page)

ledger.x: -50: the eastern Punjab belt leaves the Indo-Scythian shape (826 cells, about 208,000 km2; Cliopatria's year).
c. 10 CE: Rajuvula takes Sagala from the last Indo-Greek. 'Rajuvula conquered the last remaining Indo-Greek kingdom, under Strato II, around 10 CE, and took his capital city, Sagala'.

c. 20 CE: Gondophares founds the Indo-Parthian kingdom out of the Saka lands. 'The kingdom was founded in 19/20 when the governor of Drangiana' declared independence; 'Gondophares became the ruler of areas comprising Arachosia, Seistan, Sindh, Punjab, and the Kabul valley', 'perhaps after the death of the important…
43 CE: the Western Satraps' south is cut out.

c. 51 CE: Kujula Kadphises takes the Kabul and Gandhara country. Hou Hanshu: he 'took the Gaofu (Kabul) region' and 'defeated the whole of the kingdoms of Puda (Paktiya) and Jibin (Kapisha and Gandhara)'; the Kushans were 'gradually wresting control of the area from the Scythian tribes'. His reign is dated 25-85…

c. 75 CE: the Kushans regain the north-west. The Indo-Scythians page has the Kushans regain northwestern India c. 75 CE and the Mathura region c. 100 CE. Sa-02-b repair: Arachosia (Kandahar) and Seistan are no longer in the region; the indo-parthians dossier holds them to 226.

c. 100 CE: Mathura passes to the Kushans and the Indo-Scythian state ends. 'Mathura became part of the Kushan Empire from the reign of Vima Kadphises (90-100 CE)'; the satraps were 'probably displaced by, or became vassals of, the Kushans', and Kharapallana and Vanaspara appear as Kanishka's governors at Sarnath in c.…

wars.name: Saka invasions of Parthia
wars.outcome: between 138 and 124 BCE the Sacaraucae and Massagetae killed the Parthian kings Phraates II and Artabanus I; the Saka kept Drangiana (Sakastan).

wars.name: Mithridates II's reconquest of Sakastan
wars.outcome: Mithridates II defeated the Indo-Scythians; 'the region of Sakastan was incorporated into the Parthian Empire'; he also seized western Bactria.

wars.name: Maues' conquest of Gandhara and Taxila
wars.outcome: The Sakas took Taxila from Apollodotus II and Pushkalavati from the Indo-Greeks; Maues overstruck Archebius' and Apollodotus II's coins at Taxila.

wars.name: Vikrama's recovery of Ujjain
wars.outcome: Vikrama retook Ujjain from the Indo-Scythians and set up the Vikrama era in 58 BCE (Indo-Scythians page).

wars.name: Rajuvula's conquest of the last Indo-Greek kingdom

certainty.note: Nomad then satrap kingdoms known from coins, inscriptions and a few Greek and Chinese lines; no frontier is fixed by treaty.
